title: Representability of the dimension-filtered flatness condition for a pure module
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], quasi-coherent modules on small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $Y$ be a scheme and let $f:X\to Y$ be of finite presentation: it is quasi-compact, has quasi-compact diagonal, and is locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Let $M$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, meaning that etale locally there is an exact presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to M\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Assume $M$ is universally pure relative to $Y$ [def-sfb-space-universal-relative-purity]. Fix any integer $n\geq0$. For each scheme map $b:B\to Y$ set $X_B=X\times_YB$ and let $M_B$ be tensor pullback. Define $P_n(b)$ by requiring that for every representable etale scheme chart $a:U\to X_B$ and every $u\in U$ with image $v\in B$ satisfying $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(v)}\kappa(u)\geq n$, the stalk $(a^*M_B)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{B,v}$. Residue fields and their induced field maps are [def-weil-residue-field], transcendence degree is [def-kun-transcendence-degree], and stalkwise base-flatness is [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. There exist an algebraic space $E_n$ and a morphism $j_n:E_n\to Y$ of finite presentation which is a monomorphism, meaning that $E_n(H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H,Y)$ is injective for every scheme $H$, such that for every scheme $B$ the induced map $E_n(B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(B,Y)$ is a bijection onto $\{b:B\to Y\mid P_n(b)\}$. No proper-support assumption on $M$ or separatedness assumption on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CX1 (theorem-flat-dimension-n-representable), specialized to a scheme base and universal purity (which implies the pure hypothesis); chart formulation of flatness in dimensions at least n: Tags 0CWS (lemma-pre-flat-dimension-n) and 0CWT (definition-flat-dimension-n).

proof.text: For every $r\geq0$ form $F_r(B)=\{b:B\to Y\mid P_r(b)\}$. The base-change and sheaf theorem makes this an fpqc sheaf, hence an etale sheaf. Its map to $h_Y$ is injective on every test. Directly from the inequalities, $P_r$ implies $P_{r+1}$, so $F_r\subseteq F_{r+1}$. Restricting to any base test gives exactly the functor of the pulled-back family, since iterated tensor pullbacks and fibre products have the same defining universal properties.

We will glue local representations as follows. Let $H\subseteq A$ be an etale sheaf subfunctor of an algebraic space $A$, and choose an etale scheme covering $T_i\to A$ on which $H\times_A T_i$ is represented by schemes $Z_i$. Set $Z=\coprod_i Z_i$. Given a scheme $T$ and a section of $H(T)$, injectivity into $A(T)$ identifies $T\times_H Z$ with $\coprod_i(T\times_A T_i)$: the section fixes the unique lift to each represented fibre product. These are schemes, and their projection to $T$ is surjective etale by base change of the cover. The etale-sheaf atlas theorem therefore gives that $H$ is an algebraic space. If each $Z_i\to T_i$ is of finite presentation, the resulting $H\to A$ is of finite presentation: after any etale scheme chart of $A$, apply fppf locality of finite presentation on that scheme. Monomorphy is already the injectivity of the subfunctor. This argument applies both to scheme and to algebraic-space $A$.

source.place: 0CX1, locality reduction, using algebraic-space gluing rather than scheme effectivity.

proof.text: It suffices to work over each affine open of $Y$, by the gluing argument in step 2. On an affine base choose the universal bound $D$ for chart residue transcendence degrees. For $r=D+1$ there is no chart point with transcendence degree at least $r$, on any base test. Thus $F_{D+1}=h_Y$, represented by the identity of $Y$. We prove representability and finite presentation for $r=D,D-1,\ldots,0$ by descending induction. In the induction step suppose $F_{r+1}$ is represented by a finite-presentation monomorphism $A\to Y$. It remains to represent $F_r$ over $A$ by a finite-presentation monomorphism; composing then preserves finite presentation and injectivity.

source.place: 0CX1, paragraph beginning “In particular the situation is local”.

proof.text: Choose etale affine scheme charts $T\to A$. The pulled-back family $X_T\to T$ is still of finite presentation. Its module is finitely presented because tensoring a finite matrix presentation remains a finite matrix presentation. It is universally pure: a test scheme $B\to T$ is also a test scheme over $Y$, so an impurity after this pullback would be the same impurity for $M/Y$. Finally it satisfies $P_{r+1}$ on $T$, since $T\to Y$ factors through $A=F_{r+1}$. The universal base-change property preserves this on every further test. Accordingly it is enough, by step 2, to handle a universally pure finitely presented family on an affine scheme base with $P_{r+1}$ already true.

Fix a point $t\in T$. The complete-devissage neighbourhood theorem gives an affine etale neighbourhood $(T\prime,t\prime)\to(T,t)$ and finitely many etale affine charts $h_j:W_j\to X_{T\prime}$ covering the entire fibre at $t\prime$. Each $W_j\to T\prime$ and each pulled-back module is of finite presentation, and its coordinate module has a complete algebra devissage over $t\prime$. Write $W=\bigcup_jh_j(W_j)$. Images of etale maps are open, so $W$ is open, and it is quasi-compact over the affine base because it is the image of the finite union of the affine $W_j$. The sheaves on the $W_j$ satisfy $P_{r+1}$ by etale restriction and base change. Already at this stage apply the complete-devissage flattening lemma with $d=r$ to each original affine $W_j$: it gives a scheme representative of its $P_r$ functor on an open neighbourhood $V_j$ of $t\prime$. Keep these representatives for restriction below.

For every generalization $s$ of $t\prime$, take $\xi\in\operatorname{Ass}_{(X_{T\prime})_s}(M_s)$. Universal purity, applied to the identity test of $T\prime$ and $s\leadsto t\prime$, supplies a specialization $\xi\leadsto\theta$ in the fibre at $t\prime$. That fibre is contained in the open $W$, hence $\xi\in W$. Therefore every such $s$ lies in $E=\{s\mid\operatorname{Ass}_{(X_{T\prime})_s}(M_s)\subseteq W_s\}$. The assassin-containment theorem applies because the family and module are finitely presented and $W\to T\prime$ is quasi-compact. It gives an open neighbourhood of $t\prime$ contained in $E$. Shrink to an affine open neighbourhood inside this open and all the finitely many $V_j$ of step 5. Now $W$ contains the entire relative assassin; restrict the already obtained representatives to this neighbourhood. No new complete devissage is asserted after shrinking.

source.place: 0CX1, construction of E and shrinking; 0CVV and 05LW.

proof.text: Apply assassin localization to $h:\coprod_jW_j\to X_{T\prime}$. Its image is $W$, which contains the relative assassin. On every test scheme $B\to T\prime$, the criterion for the pulled-back finite disjoint union is exactly the conjunction of the criteria for its components: each chart point belongs locally to one component, with the same stalk and residue fields. Consequently $F_r|_{T\prime}$ is the fibre product over $T\prime$ of the finitely many dimension-$r$ flatness functors for $(W_j,M_j)$. This is equality of functors on all tests, not merely equality of loci on the base.

source.place: 0CX1, use of 0CX0 and finite product reduction.

proof.text: For each $j$, use the finite-presentation scheme monomorphism already obtained in step 5 from the affine complete-devissage flattening lemma with $d=r$, restricted in step 6 to the common neighbourhood. Their finite fibre product represents the conjunction of step 7. It is a monomorphism since every component has at most one lift; it is of finite presentation by base change and composition, applied successively. If there are no charts the conjunction is true and the representative is $T\prime$ itself. Thus $F_r$ has finite-presentation scheme representatives on an etale covering of every chart $T$ of $A$.

Glue these representatives over $A$ by step 2. This yields an algebraic space representing $F_r$ and a finite-presentation monomorphism to $A$. Compose with $A\to Y$ to finish the induction step. Descending from $D+1$ proves the claim for every $r\leq D+1$; for larger $r$ the same bound gives $F_r=h_Y$. Finally glue over the affine open covering of the original $Y$. Taking $r=n$ gives $E_n$ and $j_n$. Its sections are, by the representation of the subfunctor $F_n$, exactly the maps $b$ satisfying the stated chart criterion, with unique lift for each such $b$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0CX1 (theorem-flat-dimension-n-representable), descending induction and complete-devissage localization. Etale algebraic-space gluing realizes the same locality step; universal purity is retained throughout.
